title: IB Computer Science Mock Exam Prep for November
summary: Build a focused November IB Computer Science mock exam prep plan with syllabus checks, programming drills, timed papers, error logs, and exam-day tactics.
body_markdown:
Preparing effectively for a November mock requires more than rereading notes. Strong **IB Computer Science mock exam prep** combines syllabus checking, active recall, handwritten programming, timed papers, and systematic correction. First, confirm which syllabus, topics, paper format, and programming language your school will assess, because mocks are internally created and have no universal IB scope.


A reliable four-week cycle is to diagnose weaknesses, repair gaps, practise application, and finish with realistic simulations. This guide shows SL and HL students how to use that cycle.


### Confirm which Computer Science syllabus applies


The IB is transitioning between Computer Science courses. Students completing the Diploma in the **November 2026 examination session** follow the course described in the subject brief for first assessment in 2025. Its written assessment includes Paper 1, emphasizing problem-solving and interpreting or writing Java or Python code, and Paper 2, applying theory and practice to technological contexts.


Students assessed from **2027 onward** follow the revised course organized around **Theme A: Concepts in computer science** and **Theme B: Computational thinking and problem-solving** . Its content and assessment organization differ from the earlier course. The[official IB Computer Science course page](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/sciences/computer-science/) links to both subject briefs.


Before choosing practice materials, ask your teacher:


- Which syllabus and examination cohort applies?
- Which topics will the mock include?
- Is it a complete IB-style paper or an adapted school paper?
- Which programming language should you use?
- Are HL-only topics included?
- What time, equipment, and data booklet rules apply?


A November mock may assess only the material taught so far. Turn the confirmed scope into a checklist instead of revising every possible topic.


### Use a four-week November mock study plan


This plan assumes **60-90 minutes on five days each week** . HL students may need another weekly block for HL-only material or more complex programming.


Week Main objective Required output


Week 1 Diagnose Timed set and ranked weakness list


Week 2 Repair theory Retrieval sheets and short-answer practice


Week 3 Apply knowledge Handwritten code, tracing, and debugging


Week 4 Rehearse Timed paper, corrections, and retesting


### Week 1: Diagnose weaknesses


Complete a timed mixed set without notes. Use the correct syllabus through the[IB Computer Science Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-computer-science-new/questionbank) , a teacher-issued paper, or another syllabus-matched source.


Classify each lost mark as a **knowledge gap** , **application error** , **programming error** , **command-term error** , **timing problem** , or **careless mistake** . Rank topics by marks lost rather than perceived difficulty. A weak high-mark area deserves attention before a minor definition you already answer reliably.


### Week 2: Repair theory through retrieval


Read a short section, close the resource, and reproduce its essential ideas from memory. Looking at notes while writing creates familiarity, but it does not test whether you can retrieve information independently.


For each assessed topic, record essential definitions, one process or diagram, advantages and limitations, a practical application, and relevant security or ethical issues. The[RevisionDojo Computer Science resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-computer-science-new) connects Study Notes, Flashcards, and practice questions. Use flashcards mainly for definitions, stages, distinctions, and technical vocabulary requiring precise recall.


### Week 3: Practise programming by hand


Complete **20-30 minutes** of tracing, constructing, or debugging code on most study days. Practise selection, iteration, arrays or lists, functions, validation, searching, sorting, and object-oriented concepts required by your syllabus.


Before writing an algorithm, identify its inputs, outputs, stored data, subproblems, conditions, and test cases. When tracing, record every variable change rather than following the code mentally. Test normal, boundary, minimal, and invalid inputs because a plausible solution may still fail on an empty collection, duplicate value, or final loop iteration.


### Week 4: Simulate the mock


Complete at least one full paper, or the closest school equivalent, under strict conditions. Follow the time limit, remove your phone, and use only permitted materials.[Computer Science predicted papers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/predicted-papers/ib-computer-science) provide additional exam-style practice, but they are not forecasts of exact questions.


Mark the paper and write the missing marking point beside each important error. Explain why your answer failed, then reattempt it without copying the solution. The[IB mock exam strategy guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-mock-exam-tips-expert-strategies-for-better-performance) explains this attempt, diagnose, drill, and retest process.


### Match answers to command terms


Command terms indicate the required depth and structure:


- **State:** give a concise answer.
- **Describe:** provide relevant characteristics or an account.
- **Explain:** connect a cause or mechanism to its consequence.
- **Compare:** address relevant similarities and differences.
- **Discuss:** present a balanced, reasoned review.
- **Evaluate:** weigh strengths and limitations before reaching a justified conclusion.


Apply theory directly to the stated scenario. Rather than saying encryption “improves security,” identify the protected data, the likely threat, and the effect on the organization or users.


### Manage time according to marks


Use marks to estimate appropriate time and depth. If a paper allows 90 minutes for 75 marks, the average is approximately **1.2 minutes per mark** , although you must reserve time for reading and checking.


If stuck, record valid definitions, intermediate logic, diagrams, or working that could earn partial credit, then continue. Reserve the final **5-10 minutes** to check loop boundaries, Boolean conditions, variable updates, missing labels, unanswered parts, and contextual explanations.


### Avoid common preparation mistakes


Do not postpone questions until every topic feels revised. Exam questions expose gaps that passive review conceals. Other common mistakes include using papers from the wrong syllabus, practising code only in an editor, ignoring command terms, memorizing generic answers, and marking papers without reattempting weak questions.


If less than a week remains, follow a[focused one-week Computer Science revision plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-cram-ib-computer-science-in-1-week) . Prioritize high-mark weaknesses rather than sacrificing sleep or correction time.


### The final 48 hours


Review your error log, retrieve essential definitions, trace several short algorithms, and rewrite two or three answers that previously lost marks. Complete one timed section instead of exhausting yourself with repeated full papers. Confirm the location, start time, permitted equipment, paper length, and syllabus coverage, then stop intensive study early enough to sleep properly.


### Conclusion


Effective **IB Computer Science mock exam prep** follows a controlled sequence of diagnosis, targeted revision, programming practice, timed application, and correction. Confirm your syllabus, prioritize weaknesses by lost marks, and practise producing precise answers without notes or software support.


RevisionDojo can support this process through Study Notes, Flashcards, the Questionbank, Mock Exams, Predicted Papers, and Jojo AI. Use the tools in a consistent cycle: learn briefly, attempt independently, mark honestly, correct precisely, and retest.
